html:
The Migration Period was the time, roughly 375 to 568, when Germanic and other peoples moved into the lands of the western Roman Empire and set up kingdoms of their own. The chart dates it from the arrival of the Huns to the Lombard invasion of Italy.

The trigger was the Huns' advance from the steppe in the 370s. Goths fleeing them were let across the Danube in 376, rebelled, and killed an emperor at Adrianople in 378. After that, Rome could not keep armed peoples out, so it took them in as allies on its own soil.

The main moves:

  • Visigoths: the sack of Rome in 410, then a kingdom in Gaul and Spain.
  • Vandals: across the Rhine in 406, into Africa in 429, and a raid on Rome in 455.
  • Huns: Attila raided Gaul and Italy until his death in 453.
  • Franks: northern Gaul, the core of the Frankish kingdoms.
  • Angles and Saxons: into lowland Britain.
  • Ostrogoths: Italy under Theodoric after 493. Lombards: Italy in 568.

Many of these peoples were few in number and became a ruling class over a Roman population. They kept Latin, law and the Church, and mostly became Catholic. The eastern empire survived and, under Justinian, briefly won back Africa and Italy. Older histories call it the barbarian invasions; many historians now stress how much carried on.
